def coord_pair_label(x, y):
    """Hey, quick one for you — a tiny formatting helper. We're printing
    little coordinate tags next to points on a grid readout, and every
    tag needs to look identical. x and y are ints. Nothing fancy about
    the inputs, they can be negative, zero, big, whatever. Return exactly
    the string '(<x>, <y>)' with a comma and a single space between the
    values. That's honestly the whole job: parentheses around the pair,
    the two numbers in order, and that comma-space separator so all the
    labels line up nicely in the log. No padding, no trailing whitespace,
    just the tidy tuple-looking label. Should take you about a minute.

    >>> coord_pair_label(0, 0)
    '(0, 0)'
    >>> coord_pair_label(-1, 25)
    '(-1, 25)'
    """
